policy.certification: Only epub-33 rows describe the stable compatibility baseline. epub-34 and epub-rs-34 rows are experimental, non-certifying coverage of W3C Candidate Recommendation Drafts; they do not shift the normative baseline until promoted to Recommendation and promoted features are tested.
policy.implementedRequiresTest: A row with status implemented MUST reference at least one real test file (path exists, carries test declarations, and is picked up by the repo's test runs).
policy.nonImplementedRequiresExceptionNote: Rows with status partial, not-implemented or not-applicable MUST carry a notes entry documenting the exception, boundary, or reason.

rows.requirement: Core media type resources may be included without fallbacks; with the exception of XHTML and SVG content documents, core media type resources referenced directly from the spine MUST include manifest fallbacks (they then count as foreign content documents).
rows.notes: Media-type conformance is deferred to the isolated EPUBCheck 5.4.0 runner; reader-core does not enforce an exhaustive core-media-type table internally.

rows.requirement: All container resources live under a single root directory, and a mandatory META-INF/container.xml identifies one or more package documents (rootfiles) that define the EPUB publication.
An OCF ZIP container MUST store mimetype as the first file, uncompressed, and MUST NOT use ZIP encryption or split archives; ZIP64 is supported.
rows.notes: mimetype-first placement and archive safety nets (size caps, traversal rejection, corrupt-data rejection) are asserted; explicit split/encryption/ZIP64 rejection is not unit-tested.

rows.requirement: The package element is the required root element of the package document; its version attribute MUST be "3.0" to indicate EPUB 3 conformance, and unique-identifier is required.
The metadata element provides minimal catalog data (dc:identifier, dc:title, dc:language) and rendering metadata (meta/link, e.g. fixed-layout properties).

The manifest element lists all publication resources (container and remote) except the package document itself, which MUST NOT be self-referenced; item properties such as media-overlay drive processing.
rows.notes: Manifest items including media-overlay attributes are parsed; exhaustiveness and the no-self-reference constraint are not enforced internally (delegated to EPUBCheck).

rows.requirement: The spine element defines an ordered list of manifest itemrefs representing the default reading order, with page-progression-direction for RTL/LTR flow.
XHTML content documents MUST conform to the XML syntax and to HTML conformance criteria as constrained by this specification.
SVG content documents are core media type resources that follow the SVG specification and EPUB constrained-content requirements.
A valid EPUB navigation document MUST conform to XHTML content-document constraints and to nav element restrictions, and MUST include exactly one toc nav element.
toc, page-list and landmarks nav elements are distinguished by their epub:type value, with at most one navigation aid of each type.
Fixed-layout publications use rendition:layout=pre-paginated; each fixed-layout document represents one page, with spread/placement properties per viewport.
Media overlay documents conform to the SMIL-based media overlays schema and reference EPUB content documents for synchronized audio narration.
EPUB 3 accessibility builds on WCAG 2 and on EPUB Accessibility metadata (EPUB Accessibility 1.1 Recommendation baseline).
rows.notes: Accessibility metadata is parsed, preserved and asserted (schema:accessibilityFeature markers and explicit non-certification wording); it is descriptive only and not audited against the whole publication. No accessibility certification is implied.

rows.requirement: EPUB creators should use stable/secure links, avoid third-party and remote resources, and limit exfiltration vectors; reading systems mitigate the corresponding threats.
The EPUB 3.4 core media type list adds AVIF and JPEG XL images, and Opus-in-MP4 and AAC LC audio codecs since EPUB 3.3.
rows.notes: New codecs render through the host browser engines when natively supported; the app adds no internal codec enforcement. Experimental, non-certifying CRD coverage.

rows.requirement: EPUB 3.4 restructures layouts into reflowable, pre-paginated and the new roll layout; spread placement properties apply only to pre-paginated documents.
rows.notes: Pre-paginated support carries over from the 3.3 baseline; the new roll layout (continuous scroll) and its properties are not implemented. Experimental, non-certifying.

rows.requirement: XHTML content documents MUST use the XML syntax; support for the HTML syntax was removed in EPUB 3.4.
rows.notes: Content documents are parsed with XML-serialization expectations; an explicit rejection test for HTML-syntax documents is absent. Experimental, non-certifying.

rows.requirement: EPUB 3.4 retains SSML attributes, pronunciation lexicons and CSS Speech as valid but under-specified TTS technologies; no playback is mandated.
rows.notes: No TTS engine is integrated; the reader does not consume SSML/pronunciation lexicon/CSS Speech markup. Experimental, non-certifying.

rows.requirement: Media overlays move under Aural rendering with the same SMIL document model as EPUB 3.3 section 9.
rows.notes: Experimental non-certifying CRD row; behavior matches the EPUB 3.3 media-overlay implementation.

rows.requirement: Custom rendering properties MUST NOT be defined with a rendition: prefix and MUST NOT conflict behaviorally with the package rendering vocabulary.
rows.notes: The app defines no custom rendering properties and neither consumes nor emits them. Experimental, non-certifying.

rows.requirement: Content fallbacks, font obfuscation, the collection element and legacy package features are outdated (allowed but not recommended); SHA-1-based font obfuscation is being phased out.
rows.notes: The app does not rely on outdated features; font obfuscation is not supported; the pinned EPUBCheck 5.4.0 flags outdated-construct usage. Experimental, non-certifying.

rows.requirement: Security and privacy recommendations including watermarking considerations remain creator-side responsibilities; reading systems mitigate corresponding threats.
rows.notes: The EPUB 3.3 sanitizer policies carry over verbatim; watermarking and additional 3.4 privacy considerations are informational only. Experimental, non-certifying.

rows.requirement: Reading systems do not have to load publications or resources that violate content authoring or processing requirements.
If a reading system has a viewport it MUST support image core media type resources; if it renders prerecorded audio it MUST support audio core media type resources.
rows.notes: Image core media types render in Chromium/WebKit; prerecorded audio support is limited to media-overlay clips (playback beyond SMIL timing is out of scope).

rows.requirement: Reading systems MUST prevent data URLs from opening in top-level browsing contexts.
Reading systems MUST prevent access to resources referenced via file URLs.
Reading systems MUST use a non-validating XML processor that does not read external DTD subsets and conforms to XML namespace rules.
rows.notes: Parsing uses the platform's non-validating XML/DOMParser; external DTD subset fetching is prevented by the no-network worker design and parser timeouts, but an explicit external-DTD unit assertion is absent.

rows.requirement: For http/https links, reading systems SHOULD obtain the user's consent and open the link in a new browser instance so browser security/privacy controls apply.
rows.notes: Outbound links open through the browser's standard navigation affordance; an explicit consent prompt is not implemented or asserted.

rows.requirement: Reading systems MUST assign a container root URL to the OCF abstract container, with a unique origin per user-specific instance of a publication.
Reading systems MUST treat split archives, non-Deflate compression and ZIP encryption as errors, and MUST support ZIP64 extensions.
rows.notes: Archive validation rejects corruption, path traversal, oversized and over-compressed content; explicit split/encryption/non-Deflate/ZIP64 handling is not independently asserted.

rows.requirement: Reading systems MUST strip and collapse ASCII whitespace in Dublin Core and meta values, MUST recognize the first dc:title as the main title, and MUST process language expectations.
rows.notes: Title/language extraction and presentation are asserted; explicit whitespace-collapse semantics are not unit-tested.

rows.requirement: Reading systems MUST ignore values of the properties attribute they do not recognize, and SHOULD NOT use linked resources in rendering.
Reading systems MUST render the publication in spine order, recognizing the first primary (linear) itemref as the beginning of the default reading order.
Reading systems MUST support reflowable layouts (default) and pre-paginated layouts, producing exactly one page per spine itemref when rendering fixed layouts.
Reading systems with a viewport MUST render XHTML content documents via CSS and MUST support TrueType/OpenType/WOFF/WOFF2 font resources referenced from @font-face rules.
rows.notes: Visual CSS rendering and writing-mode/direction properties run on Chromium/WebKit; embedded font format coverage (@font-face WOFF/WOFF2) is not explicitly asserted.

rows.requirement: Reading systems SHOULD support scripting, including container-constrained scripting in reflowable content documents.
rows.notes: Implemented as an explicit security posture: scripts and inline handlers are stripped by the sanitizer and iframe-sandboxed; no script execution is offered.

rows.requirement: Reading systems MUST process EPUB navigation documents: expose toc nav links and headings, and navigate to listed page breaks when a page-list nav element is present.

Reading systems with audio capability SHOULD support media overlays: discover them via manifest media-overlay attributes, start playback at the clip corresponding to the content start, and track reading progress.
Reading systems MUST attempt to process publications whose package version attribute is less than "3.0" and SHOULD support them per their own specifications.
Reading systems SHOULD attempt to process publications whose package version attribute is greater than "3.0".
rows.notes: Unknown newer versions are tolerated structurally (the epub34-preview fixture asserts baseline rendering under a 3.0-versioned package, not a >3.0 version), but there is no dedicated forward-compat assertion.

rows.requirement: Reading system developers SHOULD specify the data they collect, seek user consent, and treat persistent personal data as sensitive.
rows.notes: The app is offline-first and stores reading data locally; explicit consent/collection documentation is not implemented.
